correctness.rationale: Verified from the accessible 2000 Main Theorem that diagonal separation and cover-edge linear-combination criteria are iff generation. Every fixed binary diagonal d has exactly q^{c(d)} idempotents by explicit unipotent conjugation and stabilizer counting; crossing cover entries vary independently and uniformly under elementary conjugations. On each cover, the forbidden coefficient vector is the q-element line spanned by the nonzero diagonal-difference vector, yielding q^h-q; noncovers contribute q^h. Summation proves the formula for any prime power, including characteristic two. Eleven independent brute-force configurations over F2/F3 passed. Small tests are not treated as infinite certification.

originality.rationale: The inspected full Longstaff–Rosenthal text gives a qualitative universal generation theorem and the inspected Khripchenko–Novikov text gives diagonal idempotent conjugacy. The 2024 Kolegov abstract gives the minimum generator threshold, not a stated exact count. Our claim is the complete fiber count and resulting probability for every finite poset, q and ordered tuple length, distinct from the known positivity/existence criterion. No equivalent result was located in actual indexed-published-finding queries; this is best-knowledge priority only. The inaccessible full 2024 article is an explicitly material residual risk.
residual_risks: Full Kolegov 2024 article (DOI 10.1017/S0004972724000078) was not accessible, so its possible unstated enumeration result could overlap.

value.rationale: A previously qualitative threshold becomes an exact natural enumeration and random-generation probability for arbitrary finite posets and all finite fields. The formula isolates local Hasse-cover obstructions and higher-comparability multiplicities, with nontrivial values for chains and forks. This is a motivated complete count of idempotent algebra generating tuples, not a choice of an arbitrary finite slice or mere restatement of minimum generator number.
